newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures end first 1997 session down.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures end first 1997 session down.

text.p: The key September three-month Euroyen futures contract ended the first session of 1997 lower on Monday in line with falls in long-term yen bond prices.
The market was also technically bearish after the contract sank below chart support points late last year, traders said.
The September ended at 99.19 after moving between 99.18 and 99.21 against the previous settlement of 99.25 on December 30.

"Many people were sidelined most of the day," said a city bank dealer. "Although the contract's fall stopped short today, there is a downside risk because people are afraid of 'triple weakness' in the Tokyo financial markets," he said.

A lack of confidence in Japan's economic strength kept market participants edgy, fanning concern over triple weakness in Japanese financial markets in which the yen is sold as capital flows out of Japanese stocks and bonds.
The dollar started 1997 in a bullish tone and briefly climbed to 117.00 yen, its highest level since March 29, 1993.

The Nikkei stock average was also initially dragged down by the yen's fall against the dollar, losing as much as 150 points before bouncing back to end at 19,446.00, up 85 points. The key 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended the first session of 1997 at a seven-week low.

Some traders said the JGB market was somewhat depressed by talk that a Japanese television station had reported during the New Year break that the Bank of Japan may raise interest rates before April. The same report, which many traders here said they ignored, pushed down the September Euroyen contract to 99.15 while the Tokyo market was closed for the holidays.
Traders said a fall to 99.15 could continue all the way down to 99.07 while the contract's topside was capped at 99.25.
Earlier this morning, the Bank of Japan conducted a neutral money market operation, which was what the market had expected.

In the cash market, the key overnight call rate rose to around 0.48 percent from 0.44 previously. Traders said the rate rise was expected after it fell on the last day of 1996 due to technical factors. Some 20 billion yen of the key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) was issued at 0.52 percent, slightly down from the previous 0.53 percent. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk (81-33432-8570)
